newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power retreats ahead of milder temps.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power retreats ahead of milder temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast retreated from Monday's inflated levels Tuesday, as temperatures were forecast to moderate through Thursday in the region.
"Prices are down today, but unless gas softens prices shouldn't fall that much further anytime soon," one market source said.

Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be about five to 15 degrees below normal early Wednesday but then turn milder through Thursday. Another cold front is forecast to pressure temperatures starting on Friday and continuing through early next week.

Firm, peak power prices in the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Wednesday fell into the $26.00-27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) area as the mildest temperatures of the week would likely arrive Wednesday.
These prices compare with Monday's range of $34.50-35.50.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices in TVA for Wednesday were assessed about a $1 lower at $16.00.
February firm, peak prices into TVA hovered around $23.00 per MWh, traders said.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks for Wednesday delivery settled into the $26.00-30.00 range, down from Monday's range of $35.00-36.00.
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally steady in a wider range of $17.00-22.00.

Seasonable temperatures in Florida kept most buyers away from the market. Temperature lows in the 40s are forecast later this week in northern Florida, which may result in the return of some buying interest.
Spot natural gas prices held steady today along the Gulf Coast around $4.00 per million British thermal units.
